answer.generated: In distributed systems engineering, two critical design issues are transparency and openness. Transparency refers to the extent to which a distributed system appears to the user as a single cohesive entity, influencing user experience and ease of interaction. Openness concerns the design of the system using standard protocols that promote interoperability versus more specialized protocols that offer greater design freedom but may limit flexibility and compatibility with other systems. These considerations directly impact the perceived unity and functionality of the distributed system from both user and developer perspectives, balancing between seamless integration and design flexibility.
